\[ H(X) = -\sum_{x \in X} p(x) \log_2 p(x) \]

- The summation is over all possible values of x in the random variable X.

The expected value of \(\log_2(1/p(X))\) is:

\[ E[\log_2(1/p(X))] = \sum_{x \in X} p(x) \log_2 \left(\frac{1}{p(x)}\right) \]

This can be simplified as:

\[ E[\log_2(1/p(X))] = -\sum_{x \in X} p(x) \log_2 p(x) \]

Which is exactly the definition of entropy H(X). Therefore, the relationship between entropy H(X) and the expected value of \(\log_2(1/p(X))\) is:

\[ H(X) = E[\log_2(1/p(X))] \]

This matches option (B).
